Photograph: Maxton Kanhema/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Passengers rescued from the ferry that capsized on Tuesday on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba. Photograph: Maxton Kanhema/AFP/Getty Images Zimbabwe At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake Rachel Savage and agencies Wed 12 Aug 2026 08.21 EDT First published on Wed 12 Aug 2026 06.34 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe , police said. The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales. A crew member told the national broadcaster ZBC that there were 153 people onboard when the ferry overturned on Tuesday after it hit large waves. A passenger told ZBC that the boat began taking on water about 30 minutes after it left the lakeshore town of Kariba, heading for islands and fishing camps. A specialised underwater team was flown to the area, the CPU said, as search and rescue continued on Wednesday. At the time, the CPU said the death toll was 15, with 27 known to be missing. Zimbabwe’s police updated the death toll on Wednesday afternoon in posts on X twice in the space of 32 minutes. In the first post , it said the death toll was 38, adding: “The bodies have been retrieved from the lake.” Then it said that 44 people were now known to have died. A video shared by ZBC on Tuesday showed several people appearing to be sitting on the upturned ferry, while at least four speedboats came to their aid and a helicopter circled overhead. Maxwell Kanhema Page, who describes himself as a media practitioner and originally posted the video shared by ZBC, reshared a video on his Facebook page filmed from the shore, in which he had noted that the lake was “angry”. He said: “A few moments later I get over 200 calls about [the ferry] sinking. A sad day indeed.” Lake Kariba is the world’s largest human-made lake by volume, stretching about 150 miles along Zimbabwe’s northern border with Zambia. It was created in the 1950s during British colonial rule, when the Zambezi River was dammed, displacing about 57,000 people. The Kariba dam supplies at least a third of both countries’ electricity. It is not uncommon for boats to overturn on the lake. In 2014, 26 people, 24 of them children, drowned in Zambia’s part of the lake, when the boat meant to transport them to independence day celebrations capsized. On the Zimbabwean side, five drowned in a 2021 incident and three were feared dead in an October 2023 capsizing. The month before, a police boat overturned although no one died. Agence France-Presse contributed to this report. US President Donald Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi first announced negotiations for the US-India Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) in February 2025. But strained ties and global conflicts have delayed negotiations, with the talks only restoring momentum this year. In February, Washington and New Delhi released the framework for an interim trade agreement. Under the deal, India will "eliminate or reduce tariffs" on all US industrial products and a wide range of US food and agricultural goods. The US agreed to reduce Trump's tariffs from 25% to 18% and rescind the punitive extra 25% tariff imposed on India for its purchase of Russian oil. But negotiations on the final deal were deferred after the US Supreme Court struck down the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs. https://countercurrents.org/2026/09/the-.text: The Only Terrorist State: Why Israel Stands Alone in a Category of Its Own in Palestine by Laala Bechetoula 14/09/2026 “The most effective way to destroy a people is to deny and obliterate their own understanding of their history.” — George Orwell “If I must die, you must live, to tell my story.” — Refaat Alareer, Gaza, November 2023 “We did not come into this world to ask permission to exist.” — Mahmoud Darwish The World Has Lists, but Only One Name. I write from Laghouat. From the city that France massacred in December 1852 and decorated its officers for. From the ground where, in a single week, an estimated three thousand of my city’s six thousand inhabitants were killed by Colonel Pélissier’s forces — the same Pélissier who, two years earlier at the Dahra caves, had ordered the burning of fires at the cave entrances until the men, women, and children sheltering inside suffocated and died. I know what it sounds like when a state kills a people and calls it civilization. I know that language in all its dialects. I have been studying it for thirty years. I am writing this because the world has run out of time for careful silences. Every year, the United States Department of State publishes its list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations. The European Union maintains its own. The United Nations Security Council keeps its consolidated register. Between them, they have designated hundreds of entities: militias, cells, networks, fronts — names that fill intelligence briefs and legal indictments, names that justify drone strikes from the Sahel to the Hindu Kush. The machinery of designation is vast, meticulous, and permanently operational. But in all these lists, there is a conspicuous absence. There is no list of terrorist states. The category does not officially exist. It does not exist for one reason only: because creating it would require naming the one state that has done more, over more decades, against more civilian populations, with more institutional protection and more calculated impunity, than any non-state actor in recorded history. That state is Israel. This is not a polemic. It is a reckoning. It proceeds from facts, from law, from the documented findings of the world’s own institutions — and from the conviction that to know a thing and refuse to name it is, in this particular moment, a form of participation in the crime. The Definition That Condemns Let us begin with the law itself — the very instruments Western governments have written, ratified, and selectively enforced against others for decades. Under United States Code, Title 18, Section 2331, international terrorism is defined as acts dangerous to human life that appear intended to intimidate or coerce a civilian population, or to influence the policy of a government by intimidation or coercion.¹ The United Nations General Assembly, in Resolution 49/60 of December 1994, defines terrorist acts as criminal acts intended or calculated to provoke a state of terror in the general public, a group of persons, or particular persons for political purposes.² Apply these definitions without political filter — without the selective blindness that governs the chancelleries of Washington, Paris, Berlin, and London — and the conclusion is not a matter of opinion. It is a matter of logic. The deliberate and systematic targeting of civilian populations, hospitals, schools, water infrastructure, refugee shelters, and markets, carried out not in error, not in isolated incidents, but as a documented, repeated, and strategically formulated policy, constitutes terrorism. Not metaphorically. Legally. By the exact definition these governments themselves wrote. The distinction between a terrorist organization and a terrorist state is not one of nature. It is one of scale, resources, and protection. An organization plants a bomb. A state drops a two-thousand-pound one on a hospital. An organization hides in basements. A state sits under the arc-lights of the United Nations General Assembly — and vetoes its own condemnation. The crime is identical. The impunity is the difference. And in international law, impunity is not an extenuating circumstance. It is an aggravating one. Terror as Doctrine Israel’s violence against civilians is not accidental. It is not the product of rogue commanders or the fog of war. It is doctrinal. It has a name, a manual, and a chain of command that reaches to the cabinet table. In military theory, it is called the Dahiya Doctrine — named for the southern Beirut suburb Israel reduced to rubble in 2006. Its author is Gadi Eisenkot, then Northern Command chief of the Israel Defense Forces. In October 2008, Eisenkot gave an interview to Haaretz in which he described the doctrine with the clarity of a man who expected no consequences: “We will apply disproportionate force on [a village] and cause great damage and destruction there. From our standpoint, these are not civilian villages, they are military bases… This is not a recommendation. This is a plan. And it has been approved.” — General Gadi Eisenkot, Haaretz, October 2008³ Read those words again. This is not a rogue commander improvising on the battlefield. This is a plan. Approved. At the level of the state. Published in a newspaper. Implemented without shame. Funded without interruption by the United States government. Gadi Eisenkot went on to become Chief of Staff of the IDF. He later joined the Israeli war cabinet. The doctrine was not repudiated. It was promoted. The Hannibal Directive adds a dimension that illuminates something even darker — how Israel relates not only to its enemies, but to its own people. This directive, confirmed by Israeli military investigations and parliamentary inquiry, authorized Israeli forces to use lethal fire to prevent the capture of Israeli soldiers, even at the cost of killing those same soldiers.⁴ On October 7, 2023, the directive was invoked. Israeli investigative journalism — principally Haaretz — documented that Israeli military fire killed an unknown number of Israeli civilians and soldiers during the Hamas attack, under the principle that capture was worse than death. A state that kills its own citizens to avoid political embarrassment has not merely used terrorism. It has made terror the grammar of its own governance. It does not merely export violence. It has internalized it. The Dossier That Cannot Be Denied Since October 7, 2023, Israel has conducted a military campaign in Gaza that international law scholars, United Nations officials, and the International Court of Justice itself have characterized in terms that exceed terrorism — entering the domain of genocide. What follows is not a list of allegations. It is a summary of documented, verified, institutional findings, assembled from the archives of the world’s own humanitarian agencies. The record speaks. Let it be heard. Hospitals. By mid-2026, Israel had struck over one hundred medical facilities in a territory that possessed only thirty-six functional hospitals before October 7. Al-Shifa Medical Complex, Gaza’s largest hospital, was raided, besieged, and systematically destroyed across multiple operations. Al-Ahli Arab Hospital was struck in October 2023. Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis was surrounded and rendered inoperable. The WHO Director-General, Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, stated without diplomatic ambiguity: “Health care should never be a target. These attacks must stop.”⁵ They did not stop. They continued, systematically, with precision munitions supplied by NATO member states. Striking hospitals is not a side effect of urban warfare. Under the Geneva Conventions, it is a war crime. Journalists. The Committee to Protect Journalists documented the killing of over one hundred and seventy journalists in Gaza since October 2023 — the highest single-conflict press death toll in CPJ’s four-decade history.⁶ These were not battlefield accidents. Issam Abdallah, a Reuters cameraman working in southern Lebanon, was killed by Israeli tank fire while wearing a clearly marked press vest. An Amnesty International investigation concluded: “The strikes were directly targeted at journalists.”⁷ Targeting journalists is not collateral damage. It is the systematic elimination of witnesses. A state that kills the people who document its crimes is a state that knows, with full lucidity, what it is doing — and intends to continue doing it without a record. Children. And here I must slow down. Because statistics, however devastating, can become anesthetic. Let me give the number first, and then give one name. UNICEF reported that more children were killed in Gaza in the first year of the offensive than in all global conflict zones combined in any single year of the previous decade.⁸ As of April 2026, over seventeen thousand children had been confirmed killed — with thousands more under rubble, uncounted, unnamed. Seventeen thousand. Repeat that number until it stops feeling abstract. Now: Hind Rajab. Six years old. On January 29, 2024, Hind was trapped in a car surrounded by the bodies of five family members who had been shot dead. She was alive. She called the Palestine Red Crescent emergency line. Her voice was recorded. She said: “Come take me. I am so scared. Please come.” The PRCS dispatched an ambulance. The crew — paramedics Yousef Zeino and Ahmed Al-Madhoun — communicated their route and mission. They drove toward a six-year-old child who was still alive and asking for help. They were killed. Their ambulance was destroyed. Hind was killed. The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor and the Hind Rajab Foundation documented the sequence: the coordinates, the Israeli military positions, the timeline, the communications.⁹ The Israeli military knew the ambulance was coming. They knew a child was waiting. They fired anyway. I do not have a legal word large enough for what that is. I have only the word that the twentieth century gave us at Nuremberg, at the Genocide Convention, at the foundational documents of the international order this same West claims to defend. Famine as a weapon. Michael Fakhri, UN Special Rapporteur on the Right to Food, stated in March 2024: “Israel is using starvation as a method of warfare. This is a war crime.”¹⁰ The World Food Programme confirmed near-famine conditions in northern Gaza as early as February 2024.¹¹ Aid convoys were blocked, bombed, and turned back. On February 29, 2024 — a date that will be entered in the ledgers of history — Israeli forces opened fire on a crowd of civilians gathered at the Nabulsi roundabout in Gaza City, waiting for food. Over one hundred people were killed. They were holding bags. They were hungry. They were shot.¹² Infrastructure. UNEP estimated by mid-2025 that eighty percent of Gaza’s buildings had been damaged or destroyed.¹³ Water desalination plants were systematically targeted. UNICEF warned that the collapse of the water system would kill more children than the bombs. The UNDP calculated the total material damage at over forty billion dollars — the accumulated construction of decades, erased in months.¹⁴ What remains is not a battlefield. It is the archaeological site of a civilization that was deliberately ended. Future historians will dig through this rubble the way we dig through Pompeii. The difference is that Pompeii was a natural disaster. The Court Has Spoken. The Killing Continued. On January 26, 2024, the International Court of Justice — the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, founded from the ruins of the Second World War precisely to prevent its repetition — issued provisional measures in South Africa v. Israel, brought under the Genocide Convention. The Court ruled, by a vote of fifteen to two, that the rights of Palestinians in Gaza to be protected from genocide were plausible under the Convention.¹⁵ Plausible genocide. Not the words of a protest movement. Not the words of a government that can be accused of partisanship. The words of the court the world built — from the ashes of Auschwitz, from the rubble of Warsaw, from the mass graves of Europe — to ensure that the words never again carried legal force. The court the Western world cites when it suits it, and ignores when it doesn’t. The Court ordered Israel to take all measures within its power to prevent acts that could fall under the Genocide Convention, including killing members of the group, causing serious bodily or mental harm, and deliberately inflicting conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction in whole or in part. The morning after that order, Israeli forces bombed a hospital in Rafah. The United States exercised its veto at the Security Council — for the fourteenth time in a decade — to shield Israel from a binding resolution. No consequences followed. No sanctions. No arms embargo. The weapons kept flowing. The bombs kept falling. The children kept dying. When a state defies an order of the International Court of Justice with absolute impunity — and the world watches and does nothing — we have not merely failed international law. We have abolished it. What remains is not a rules-based international order. It is a protection racket wearing a United Nations badge. The Architects of Impunity A terrorist state cannot survive without infrastructure. The infrastructure of Israel’s impunity was not improvised. It was constructed, over decades, with architectural precision, by a small group of Western governments that have made themselves not bystanders but accomplices — and accomplices, under the very conventions they drafted, ratified, and invoke against others, bear legal responsibility. The United States has provided Israel with over 3.8 billion dollars in annual military aid since 2016, under a ten-year Memorandum of Understanding signed by the Obama administration. Since October 7, 2023, emergency weapons packages authorized by the Biden administration exceeded 14 billion dollars in additional military hardware.¹⁶ Among the munitions delivered: the MK-84 unguided bomb, two thousand pounds of explosive, used in strikes that killed hundreds of civilians at a time — in the Nuseirat refugee camp in June 2024, in the al-Mawasi designated humanitarian zone in August 2024. Designated. Safe zone. Bombed. With American bombs. Signed by an American president. The United Kingdom continued arms exports to Israel after its own legal advisors warned, in formal government memoranda, of a clear risk of serious violations of international humanitarian law.¹⁷ The British government reviewed those warnings. It overrode them. The export licences were renewed. Germany — the Federal Republic whose entire post-war identity rests on the vow never again, whose constitution, foreign policy, and moral claim to a place among civilized nations is built on the memory of the Holocaust — approved weapons exports to Israel as the ICJ was deliberating on genocide. The Bundesrepublik Deutschland armed a state the world’s highest court found plausibly engaged in the crime Germany above all others swore to prevent. I am not able to describe this as irony. Irony implies distance. This is proximity. This is inheritance. This is what it looks like when a wound becomes a weapon in the hands of those who did not receive it. France suspended arms exports — eventually, partially, after months of international pressure, after the bodies had been counted in the tens of thousands. The gesture was noted. It was insufficient. It was late. These governments are not passive witnesses. They are the load-bearing walls of Israel’s impunity. Remove their support, and the structure collapses. They know this. They choose, every day, to keep the walls standing. That choice has a legal name. Its name is complicity. Its consequences, under the Genocide Convention these states themselves signed, are not optional. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq8e.text: Image source, Bell County Sheriff's Office/Reuters Image caption, An undated handout image of Hasan that was released by authorities in 2012 By Sareen Habeshian Published 6 October 2026 Updated 1 hour ago The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first military execution in more than 60 years. Nidal Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that US defence secretary Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it. The execution is scheduled to take place at Fort Hood in Texas on 3 December, the secretary of the US Army said on Tuesday. It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two. "Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," Parnell wrote on X. Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan. The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base. The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines. Watch: Why is America running out of execution drugs? , external Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row. A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law. It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward. The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan. Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level. The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option. Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years. Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah. Figure caption, How widely used is the death penalty in the US? Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025. Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty. The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens". https://www.politico.eu/article/patriots.text: STRASBOURG — Officials acting on behalf of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office searched the offices of staff of the far-right Patriots group in the European Parliament on Wednesday morning. The searches are part of an investigation into allegations that the now-defunct Identity and Democracy group mismanaged EU funds. In 2025, the Parliament’s finance department found that ID misspent €4.3 million between 2019 and 2024 in irregular donations and public tenders. The EPPO, which investigates financial crimes involving the EU budget, opened a probe based on the Parliament’s reports. “Since this morning, searches have been underway at the European Parliament in Strasbourg — where we are currently located — targeting the offices of staff members of the former Identity and Democracy Group,” said France’s National Rally chief in the Parliament, Jean-Paul Garraud. Advertisement Advertisement The EPPO confirmed it carried out searches in the Parliament’s buildings in France and Belgium “as part of an ongoing investigation into the use of European funds by a former political group in the European Parliament.” The searches took place at the group’s secretariat offices, according to two officials, granted anonymity to speak about the ongoing investigation. When ID dissolved in 2024, many of its staff moved to the Patriots, including lawmakers from France’s National Rally, Austria’s Freedom Party, Hungary’s Fidesz, Spain’s Vox, Belgium’s Flemish Interest and Czechia’s ANO 2011. In their statement, the group insisted “there is no legal continuity with the ID Group” and that “it is not involved in the ongoing investigations.” The allegations of mismanagement of funds relate to the budget allocated annually by the Parliament for political groups to spend on administrative and operative costs. EPPO is probing whether ID made irregular donations to regional organizations in several EU countries, and whether the group breached tender rules in contracts awarded to companies friendly to the group. In 2025, the finance department ordered the Patriots to give back €276,967 in EU funds it says the group misused during the second half of 2024, related to similar irregular tender procedures. Advertisement Advertisement “As always when requested Parliament cooperates with relevant authorities — we don’t have additional comment,” a Parliament spokesperson said via a text message.
